title: Release trapped clothing and open a drawer
instruction: Open the wooden drawer fully. First, move the left gripper to the blue drawer handle. Position the fingers on opposite sides of the handle, close the gripper around it, and pull the handle outward toward the robot bases. Keep the right arm away while the left arm grasps and begins pulling. If the drawer stops because the orange cloth is caught, keep the left gripper closed on the handle and pause pulling. Bring the right gripper to the exposed orange cloth and press it downward into the drawer. While the right gripper maintains downward pressure, continue pulling the handle with the left arm. Once the cloth clears the cabinet edge, lift the right gripper away and finish pulling the drawer fully open.
context: Study recovery from a mechanical obstruction during household manipulation: maintain control of a drawer while creating clearance around trapped clothing. The current score measures ordered recovery progress, not force compliance or comprehensive safety.
setup: Fixed layout on the built-in calibrated YAM station, with two 6-DoF arms and wrist cameras. Coordinates are metres: x away from the arm bases, y left, z up. Oak-appearance cabinet panels surround a 400 mm wide, approximately 320 mm deep wooden drawer of mass 0.50 kg, with a passive 200 mm rail and damping 12/s. Drawer origin (0.50, 0.04, 0.8125). Blue metal-appearance grasp block 26 x 32 x 26 mm, centred at (0.28, 0.18, 0.8125), on a silver stem 56 x 12 x 12 mm. Three rigid folded-clothing collision proxies are fixed inside the drawer, with linen/cotton/denim appearance. The orange textile-shaped obstruction has a declared envelope 104 x 50 x 26 mm, mass 0.04 kg, initial origin (0.486, -0.080, 0.8495), and a vertical spring: stiffness 30 N/m, damping 1.5 N s/m, travel 40 mm. A wooden lip 14 x 60 x 30 mm at (0.347, -0.080, 0.8665) blocks it. No layout jitter. README and setup_layout.json list component dimensions and positions; bundled USD assets define exact geometry.
scoring: Ordered event scoring, evaluated at episode end. Valid initial state: opening <5 mm and fold compression <5 mm. 0.25 after a jam: 98 mm < opening <120 mm, compression <9 mm, and opening changes <0.6 mm per step for 10 consecutive 20 Hz updates. 0.50 after that jam and compression >14 mm. 0.75 after that compression and opening >172 mm. 1.0 after those events and opening >=190 mm with drawer linear speed <0.01 m/s and angular speed <0.1 rad/s. Success termination requires a 1 s hold. Invalid geometry or no completed milestone scores zero. Valid geometry requires finite measured states, opening in [-2,202] mm, drawer lateral and bottom offsets <=4 mm, width/depth errors <=6 mm, fold x tracking error <8 mm, fold y error <8 mm, and fold compression strictly between -5 and 45 mm. Milestones are latched in order; full-score stillness is assessed at the current state. Scorer measures object events and does not independently require a particular arm or number of arms.
run_limit: 1,800 control steps (90 simulated seconds at 20 Hz)
reset_notes: Start a fresh process for each trial to reset the scene and scorer. Fixed layout, object_jitter=0. No consumables.
fidelity: Rigid cabinet and drawer with passive constrained motion. Folded clothing is rigid; the orange fold is a spring-supported rigid proxy, not deformable fabric. Textures do not imply deformable physics. The scripted demo uses privileged simulator state. No real-world validation or complete collision-safety certification is claimed.
